extracted.intended_audience: scholars and researchers in education preparing grant proposals for the Spencer Foundation
extracted.subtask_description: Prepare field-initiated research grant proposals for the Spencer Foundation that align with the foundation's expectations for intellectual ambition, methodological rigor, relevance, and potential impact in education research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Field-initiated research (applicant-driven topics)
rubrics_metrics.description: Our research grants are not designed for applicants to respond to a specific request – they are what you, scholars in the field, think we need to know more about.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should originate from the applicant's view of important unanswered questions in the field rather than responding to a narrowly prescriptive request; emphasize why the topic merits independent investigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigorous research
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate methodological rigor appropriate to the research questions, including clear design, valid measures, plausible causal inference (when relevant), and thorough treatment of limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intellectually ambitious work
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pose challenging, substantive questions or lines of inquiry that push conceptual or empirical boundaries in education research rather than incremental or routine studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technically sound research
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure analytic approaches, data collection, and interpretation are technically appropriate and defensible; include sufficient technical detail for reviewers to assess feasibility and validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevance to pressing questions and compelling opportunities in education
rubrics_metrics.description: Research that is relevant to the most pressing questions and compelling opportunities in education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Articulate how the proposed work addresses timely, important problems or opportunities in education and why the findings would matter to the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creative and open-minded scholarship
rubrics_metrics.description: We value work that fosters creative and open-minded scholarship
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show intellectual openness to novel theories, methods, interdisciplinary perspectives, or alternative interpretations; explain creative elements of approach or framing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement in deep inquiry
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Go beyond surface description: propose in-depth exploration of mechanisms, contexts, meanings, or processes rather than solely descriptive or narrowly scoped analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination of robust questions related to education
rubrics_metrics.description: Examines robust questions related to education
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define clearly articulated, robust research questions that are conceptually grounded and have clear implications for interpretation and further research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Development of new foundational knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: Support scholarship that develops new foundational knowledge
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how the project will contribute to foundational theory, concepts, or evidence in education research rather than only producing localized findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential for lasting impact on policy, practice, or discourse
rubrics_metrics.description: May also have a lasting impact on policy-making, practice, or educational discourse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe the pathways through which findings could influence policy, practitioner behavior, or broader academic and public conversations; emphasize potential for sustained influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: High-quality, innovative research in education broadly conceived
rubrics_metrics.description: We support high-quality, innovative research on education, broadly conceived.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Position the project as both high-quality and innovative: identify novelty (methods, theory, population, setting) and quality indicators (expertise of team, prior work, feasibility, rigor).
